transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
The U.S. and Israel are preparing plans for a possible attack on Iran in early November
after the midterm elections.
That's according to a person briefed on the matter speaking to NPR.
From Tel Aviv, NPR's Daniel Estrin has our story.
The person briefed on the U.S. and Israel's war planning spoke to NPR on condition of anonymity
to discuss the preparations.
The person said Israel had initially planned to strike Iran in mid-October
about two weeks before Israeli elections October 27th, but President Trump objected.
The person briefed said the U.S. is now amassing forces in the region to be ready for an attack
by early November, after U.S. midterms November 3rd,
but that these preparations could also be part of a campaign to pressure Iran to reach a diplomatic deal.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is campaigning for reelection on a threat to topple Iran's regime.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
American Stephen Hubbard is returning to the U.S. after he was released from a Russian prison by President Putin.
President Trump's special envoy, Steve Whitcoff, called Putin a "humanitarian."
That comment has been rebuked by a group of bipartisan U.S. lawmakers.
There's less than two weeks to go before the midterms.
President Trump is stumping through several states, campaigning for Republicans.
NPR's Stephen Fowler says Democrats are out doing the same.
In the midterm cycle, Democrats are on offense, so there are a lot of people sitting in safer blue states
and sort of purple states that are now safe that are being deployed to the competitive toss-up races
and into deep red territory where it makes sense.
And a lot of people seeking out their ideological compatriots.
For example, New York Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez going to Michigan for Abdul El-Sayed.
You've got the independent Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders for candidates in Maine, Florida, and Texas.
And, of course, the big one.
Former President Obama going to final pushes in Ohio, Michigan, Georgia.
NPR's Stephen Fowler reporting.
A serious security vulnerability in a popular programming language has website operators scrambling to protect their web pages.
NPR's Jenna McLaughlin reports news outlets and government agencies could be affected.
The language, called PHP, quietly supports components of major platforms like WordPress and Drupal.
Some estimates suggest PHP is used to power close to 70 percent of modern web pages.
Government agencies in the Netherlands and Finland, for example, took their websites offline to preempt any attacks.
Major technology companies were involved in uncovering the flaw, including OpenAI,
which said in a blog post that its model helped find the bug before attackers did.
Developers maintaining the programming language released patches to seal the hole on Wednesday.
The NSA urged organizations to take their systems down and apply the fix immediately.
Jenna McLaughlin, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR.
The Trump administration says it will loan up to 315,000 barrels of heating oil to Americans this winter.
The fuel will be exclusively used in Connecticut, Massachusetts and Maine.
Trump will tap up to one-third of the U.S. Emergency Heating Oil Reserve.
Up to a third of homes in New England need this heating oil, and prices for the fuel have skyrocketed.
A new analysis finds it takes twice as long to save up for a starter home as it did seven years ago.
NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports the focus is on a down payment and closing costs.
Many renters might be able to afford a mortgage but don't have the cash to seal the deal.
And with rising rents and other costs, it's gotten a lot harder to save up for it, says Mike Calhoun,
is with the Julian Bond Institute at the Center for Responsible Lending.
For the median renter income, that requires 16 years of savings.
At that rate, the report notes, children may have moved out before a couple can move in to a first home.
The savings time needed is less for middle income and frontline workers, like police officers and teachers,
10 to 13 years, but that's also twice as long as in 2019 before home prices and mortgage rates spiked.
Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Washington.
The Vatican says that Pope Leo's doctors report he does not need further medical treatment.
Surgeons removed part of Leo's right lung last week to treat cancer.
The Vatican says testing shows the tumor was localized and that no further treatment is needed for the pontiff.
This is NPR News.
